headline: US strikes on Iran spiked oil and knocked 721 points off the KSE-100 - the desk has flipped to risk-off, and only refiners and the strongest banks look worth watching today.
summary: US strikes on Iranian positions and Tehran's retaliation pushed Brent to $92 and knocked the KSE-100 down 721 points yesterday; the desk's macro read has flipped to risk-off. Global markets are cautious too - the S&P and Dow dipped, VIX ticked up, and gold's safe-haven bid keeps building. On PSX the reaction split cleanly: refiners rallied on wider crack spreads while autos, cement, OMCs and power all sold off. Reserves are thin (about $17bn, near 2.6 months of imports) and a hot August CPI print is still due, so the desk leans toward refiners and well-capitalized banks holding government paper, and away from anything leveraged to fuel costs or hoped-for rate relief.

sectors.name: Refineries
sectors.why: ATRL/NRL/PRL were the only sector to actually gain on yesterday's selloff, because a higher crude price widens their crack-spread economics even as it squeezes almost everyone else.

sectors.name: Large, well-capitalized banks
sectors.why: T-bill and PIB cutoffs keep grinding up (6M 11.80%, 10Y PIB 12.30%), a genuine carry tailwind for banks holding government paper into the Sept 14 rate decision - this is the large-cap end of the sector, not every bank ticker.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: OMCs are squeezed between a near-daily-reset pump price and a rising import bill for the fuel itself, and sold off with the broader market yesterday despite the same oil move that lifted refiners.

sectors.name: Autos, cement, power/IPPs
sectors.why: All three were named among yesterday's broad sellers, and power/IPPs carry the extra overhang of unresolved circular debt heading into the IMF's expected September review.

sectors.name: Small/thinly-capitalized banks
sectors.why: The pending August CPI print is forecast at 10.75-11.4% YoY even before this oil shock, arguing against pricing in the near-term rate relief that smaller, more rate-sensitive banks would need.

watchlist.angle: Two backtested strategies are currently constructive here - sma_golden_cross (4.81% net expectancy, out-of-sample hit rate 1.0 on a small sample) and triple_screen_long (1.19% net expectancy, out-of-sample hit rate 0.73) - and the fundamental card reads attractive: P/E near 5.5x, 17.4% net margin, a 10.29% dividend yield covered by a 56% payout ratio. It sits inside the large-bank sector the desk is favouring for the government-paper carry tailwind.
watchlist.risk: It's still a commercial bank heading into a hot pending August CPI print - if that number lands hawkish enough, rate-sensitive banks broadly could give back ground regardless of BAFL's individual quality.

watchlist.angle: It's the clearest live expression of the sector tilt itself - ATRL was among the lone gainers on yesterday's 721-point selloff on wider crack-spread expectations as Brent pushed to $92. Fundamentals are cheap (P/E 4.9x, forward 3.45x, improving) and there's a confirmed dividend catalyst on the calendar: Rs15/share, ex-dividend and book closure 2026-10-13.
watchlist.risk: RSI14 is already at 74.3 - overbought after the recent surge - and net margins are thin at 7.6%. A lot of the good news may already be priced in, and any pullback in Brent undercuts the whole crack-spread argument.

watchlist.angle: Fundamentals read attractive - cheap P/E (6.26x, forward 4.49x, improving), 17.1% net margin, an 8.58% dividend yield covered by a 54% payout - on top of a recent 44% profit jump and a confirmed, near-dated catalyst: ex-dividend 2026-09-10, book closure 2026-09-11, paying Rs1.6/share.
watchlist.risk: Beta of 1.2 means it swings more than the market in both directions, which cuts against you in a risk-off tape, and it's the same commercial-banking sector as BAFL above.

catalysts.event: PBS August 2026 CPI release - not yet out; independently forecast 10.75-11.4% YoY even before this oil shock
SCBPL book closure (confirmed); OGDC and PSO results due (unconfirmed)
IMF 4th EFF / 3rd RSF review mission expected - ~$1.2bn potential disbursement, circular debt the key sticking point
SBP MPC - next rate decision, now with a fresh oil-driven inflation upside risk in the mix

risks: Brent holding above $90 - if the conflict widens further, the import bill grows against reserves of only about $17.1bn (roughly 2.6 months of cover), the classic setup for PKR and reserve stress even though the rupee has held flat for 12 straight sessions so far.
The pending August CPI print, forecast at 10.75-11.4% YoY, lands right before the Sept 14 SBP decision - a hot number would undercut the 'large banks as defensive carry play' half of today's read.
The conflict is genuinely live - fresh strikes and retaliation this cycle, six months running - so today's 'moderate' 62/100 geo-risk score could re-rate higher fast on any further escalation.
